note: The properties registry: the declaration table of docs/registries.md, binding scope x property to its one authoritative registry. Registries name their carrier, key field (structural identity, exempt from declaration), target grain, scope, gate, the `area` that groups them for a reader with a `title` and a `gloss`, an optional `identity` giving the space their key resolves into for the ownership gate, and whether their per-row fields are `governed` (held to the declarations below) or `ungoverned` (declared and counted, with a written `why` naming what about the carrier the field check cannot reach). Declarations carry mode (recorded or computed, with the deriver for computed), required (what the gates enforce today: value, counted, or none), and the value domain where one is closed. Governed carriers are held both ways by tools/test/properties-registry.test.mjs: an undeclared row field fails, a declared property missing from the carrier fails, a value outside a declared closed domain fails, and a required:value property blank on any row fails (2,304 presence assertions across 52 declarations; both added after audits found the same rot, that a field nothing reads goes wrong: eight domains declared and none read, then 54 value grades unchecked and three false), a computed declaration whose deriver does not exist fails, and the ungoverned count is asserted so it can only move deliberately. Expanded 2026-08-09 from six registries to thirteen by the reconciliation recorded in docs/registries.md, which walked the estate against the model rather than the model against itself; sixteen since. All sixteen are field-governed. Five were initially declared ungoverned with written reasons and all five reasons proved wrong on inspection, so the assertion now reads zero rather than a count: `fields: ungoverned` survives only so that adding one has to change a test. Origin: budget-drs data/design/properties.csv in mehrlander/home. Three checks were added 2026-08-13. The registry row is now held to a named field set, since the index governs the carriers and nothing governed the index. The ownership rule (`target x property` resolves to at most one registry) finally has the gate its own prose promised, deciding on assertions rather than declarations so a crosswalk may declare a property it fills only where no census owns it; it found two live violations on its first run, nine `role` pairs and four `title`/`note` pairs, both resolved by inheritance rather than by renaming, which would have hidden the duplication from the gate without removing it. And tools-gallery, reshaped into a crosswalk over pages-catalog, must resolve every row to a page, since dropping a field makes a blank card possible where a stale one used to be.

registries.title: Content classification
registries.gloss: What each artifact is epistemically: supplied source material, mechanical output, or authored analysis, and which corpora it belongs to.
registries.scope: artifacts the registry curates; authoritative for what it covers, undeclared is a normal state
registries.target: an artifact, by locator (may refine below a file)

registries.title: Documentation inventory
registries.gloss: Every document under docs/, what it is about, whether it is kept true, and who can reach it.
registries.scope: every .md and .json file under docs/ (the gate walks those two extensions; docs/examples/, docs/prototypes/ and docs/favicons/ hold four other files, out of scope and deliberately so)

registries.title: Harness inventory
registries.gloss: Every code file under tools/ and scripts/, what it is for, how it is invoked, and whether prose names it or a test exercises it.
registries.scope: code files under tools/ and scripts/, except tools/test/, which the tests census owns

registries.title: Manifest field vocabulary
registries.gloss: Every key a repo’s .web-tools.json may carry, what it means, and which consumer reads it.
registries.scope: every key in use across the estate's repo manifests

registries.title: Statement ownership
registries.gloss: For a statement the coordination layer repeats, which carrier is authoritative and how every other mention relates to it.
registries.target: a repeated statement, or a scope for a family rule
registries.scope: statements the hub's coordination layer repeats; curated against the written scope in the carrier, not complete over the estate

registries.title: Page gallery
registries.gloss: Every HTML page under pages/, grouped, with the title and thumbnail the gallery and picker show.
registries.scope: every .html page under pages/, arranged into groups; the group wrapper (label, top) is structure rather than assertions about a page, the same standing as a carrier note block

registries.title: To-go set
registries.gloss: The files that travel to other repos, and how a consumer takes each one.
registries.scope: files curated to travel to other repos; an authored selection crosswalk over the censuses that own each target, so intrinsic description is inherited rather than restated

registries.title: Delivery modes
registries.gloss: How a tossed payload travels, and the trust and sandbox posture each mode carries.
registries.scope: the ways toss-render.html is handed a payload or a reference, and the trust posture each buys

registries.title: Renderer dispatch table
registries.gloss: Every route toss-render accepts, what each one addresses, and which viewer it opens.
registries.scope: the content types that map to a renderer page; owner of toss-render.html's inlined TOSS_ROUTES literal

registries.title: Showing mechanisms
registries.gloss: Which link reaches which kind of change, and what each one silently misses.
registries.scope: the links that can show a change, what each reaches and misses; rendered as the Map view Showing tab

registries.title: Skill roster
registries.gloss: The skills this repo ships, each carrying the trigger description its own SKILL.md owns.

registries.title: Surfacing primitives
registries.gloss: The gated index of SURFACING.md’s primitives, the prose staying authoritative.
registries.scope: the primitives SURFACING.md defines. The PROSE stays authoritative and this is its gated index, so ownership runs opposite to every other registry here; declaring its fields governs the INDEX, not the definitions

registries.title: Test coverage map
registries.gloss: Every check in the suite, what kind it is, and what breaks if it is deleted.
registries.scope: every .mjs under tools/test/ except the declared shared helpers

registries.title: Prose field vocabulary
registries.gloss: The sanctioned names for a prose-bearing field, so one concept is not called four things across four carriers.
registries.scope: the names a prose-bearing CSV column or JSON key may carry, estate-wide; portable, since a concept named once should be the same concept in every repo

registries.title: Tools shelf
registries.gloss: The authored selection of pages the Tools view shows, and the icon each is given; a crosswalk over the page gallery.
registries.scope: pages the Tools view shelves; a crosswalk over pages-catalog, which owns each page's title and description. Every bare hub path must resolve to a row in pages/pages.json

registries.title: Tracker board
registries.gloss: Every task in the project tracker, its state, size, and activity, derived from the task files.

registries.title: App route inventory
registries.gloss: Every destination the show-repo app can be sent to, what it is for, and which files draw it.
registries.scope: the ?view= keys show-repo.html's VIEWS table dispatches, and the files that render each; not toss routes, which are a content type mapped to a renderer page and answer to routes-routes

declarations.gloss: what the document is about, one line
whether the document is kept true, preserved as written, or derived from measurement
who can get to the document: injected at session start, reachable from project instructions, a skill, the app, or nothing
the document's size, and its share of the folder
who keeps the document true; a bare row is counted by the census rather than hidden
the genre of check; the vocabulary is closed and the gate holds rows to it
the one thing that breaks if the test is deleted; blanks are counted

how many assertions the file makes. Blank, never zero, on the 10 browser-driven checks that are not node:test files, because test() is not their unit; the blank is the honest reading and the count is the ledger figure

what each top-level test() call is named, in source order; the file's own account of its coverage, so protects need not restate it. A parameterized name is carried as its template text. Blank on the same 10 browser-driven checks as its count, for the same reason: test() is not their unit
how the check reaches its subject, strongest present wins
suite for a *.test.mjs file, else the npm script that runs it, else unrun

which assertions only check a component mounts, as indices into assertion_names; the property is per assertion, so a file-level count is the length rather than the record. Blank on the same 10 browser-driven checks, for the same reason
what the file is for; blanks are counted rather than hidden
which shelf the file sits on. The domain is closed and owned by the carrier's own layers glossary block, the same arrangement as manifest-fields.consumer; docs/code-layers.md is the prose behind it
file length

how the file gets run: argv, imported, driver, 'none found' (the warning state), or npm:<script> naming the script. Deliberately OPEN, because the npm form is a grammar rather than an enumeration and a new script must not need a declaration edit
writes a file: a generator rather than a reader
its path or basename appears in tracked prose
a file under tools/test/ exercises it
what the artifact IS epistemically; the portable content-registry skill owns the convention
what the artifact is good for downstream. The domain is closed and is owned by the content-registry skill, not here; docs/owners.json records the copy
one line on the artifact
what species of thing travels
the invocation name; present on kind:skill rows only
display name

what the item does for an adopting repo. NOT asserted where a census already owns the claim: blank on the nine scripts harness-census describes, joined at render time. Kept on the skills, whose skills-catalog row carries a model-facing trigger description rather than a reader's one-liner
how a consumer takes the item: installed by the plugin, read live, referenced, adopted once, or fetched on demand
phosphor icon name
whether the row owns one repeated statement or declares a rule over a scope; a family row is a DECLARATION in this model, carried here because its carrier is distributed
the population a family rule covers; absent on a statement row
the one carrier that owns the statement; every other mention is a repetition
each other place the statement appears, with its relation (copy, paraphrase, pointer, live read), who keeps a copy, and the check that holds it or the honest absence of one
the skill's trigger description. A COPY: the authoritative carrier is the skill's own SKILL.md, per the family rule in docs/owners.json
the short name the catalog card and the picker show
the page's own <title>, read from the file
the one-line blurb. Authored in the NOTES map inside the deriver, not here, and blank on 42 of 69 pages: a counted figure, the honest measure of how much of the gallery is unexplained
the committed screenshot path; refreshed once per session, never by the commit hook
the GitHub blob URL for the page source
the task's short imperative, read from its frontmatter
where the task sits. Domain owned by docs/TRACKER.md
the date the task was filed
the date it was completed; absent while open, which is not a blank to count
the task file this row is derived from
the blob URL the board and the caption link to

the date of the newest progress-log line. Blank on a task filed without one, which the board generator allows and the tasks template does not produce; the blank is the honest reading of 'filed, nothing logged yet' and is worth counting
how many progress-log lines the task carries
the branch that owns the task while it is in progress, or completed it
the workspace a task belongs to, where the repo scopes them
effort calibrated to the session. Domain owned by docs/TRACKER.md; optional by design, and carried on 9 of 75
the dependency or workstream tag, including depends-on: pointers
open tags preserved from the frontmatter and not acted on
free text naming what is holding the task; cleared by hand
the task or condition a blocked row names
the address shape, e.g. #gz=<base64url of gzipped HTML>
whether the payload rides in the URL or is fetched
how the renderer treats what arrives. n/a is the data route, which hands bytes to a viewer rather than executing a page, so the question does not arise
the sandbox the mode renders under
who can open it: any reader, or a token holder
what the mode buys and what it costs
the repo holding the renderer page
the ref the renderer is read at
the renderer page
the content type this route is for
the envelope contract the route honors
a worked address
the marker the caption uses
the mechanism name a reader sees
the address shape; absent where the mechanism is not a URL
what kind of thing it can show
which version of the subject it reaches
who can open it
what it does show
what it does NOT show, which is the field the picker turns on
the failure mode, where one has bitten; carried on 1 of 7
when to pick it
the bullet lead-in, held two-way against SURFACING.md's prose
the short name
the caption marker; blank on 9 of 20, which have no marker of their own
what the primitive is for, in one line
where it stops working; carried on 14 of 20
the concrete shape, where the primitive has one
the JSON type the key takes
which reader acts on the key. Domain owned by the carrier's own consumers block
what the key does and who owns its value
set only where a key is superseded but still parsed
the shape of a nested object or array key
who the text under this field name is addressed to; the split that decides whether it belongs in a carrier or in source
what this field name means, in a sentence
the rule for picking this name over its neighbours, which is the part a definition alone never settles
the names already in use that this one accounts for; the survey resolves them rather than reporting them as violations, so an existing carrier conforms by declaration rather than by rename
the URL shape that opens it, e.g. ?view=map
its name in the nav and on the row
which context it is reached from
what the destination is for, one line

the files that render it, shell excluded. Blank is a finding, not a gap: three routes render from components defined inline in the shell and so have no code of their own, which the Routes pane counts rather than hides
why a row has no files, or what qualifies the row
a retired key that still resolves
the sub-tabs addressable within it

the nav destination it is reached as. Six sub-tabs are addressed as their own ?view= key while twelve are addressed as ?view=<parent>&tab=, so this is the level the router flattens away; the gate holds every estate route's value to estateNav
